run: frankenstein_stepC stitch (step C: widen the backend block b5 by stitching the top two Step B champions over the commonized trunk)

step1_champion_search.population: final population of the Step B run (checkpoint.npz, 100 genomes, all sharing the frozen 788-gene trunk, differing only in b5)

champion_2.definition: best validation gap among genomes not bit-identical to champion #1

stitch.trunk: embed + blocks b0..b4 + merged decoder, 788 genes, kept ONCE, bit-exact from champion #1 (the same trunk in both parents - the common ancestor, not duplicated)

widened_block_b5w.position: after the joining block (b4), before the merged decoder - replaces b5
widened_block_b5w.attention: 2 heads; head 0 = champion #1's b5 head, head 1 = champion #2's b5 head; head outputs summed into the stream, each head adding its own W_o and b_o; every entry bit-exact
widened_block_b5w.ffn: width 8; units 0-3 = champion #1's (W_1 columns 0-3, W_2 rows 0-3, b_1[0:4]), units 4-7 = champion #2's (W_1 columns 4-7, W_2 rows 4-7, b_1[4:8]); every entry bit-exact
widened_block_b5w.shared_layer_norms: lnA and lnF are champion #1's genes
dropped_from_champion_2: b5.b_2 (the FFN output bias is a single block-level parameter, like the layer-norms: champion #1's is used)
widened_block_b5w.rescaling: none - no weight is halved or rescaled; there are no filler entries in this stitch

gene_accounting.rule: backbone = the 788 trunk genes; stitching = ALL genes of the widened block b5w, which must now be refined as a unit

birth_gap_note: two branches' outputs now sum into the same stream with no rescaling, so a birth gap worse than champion #1's 7.9739% is expected
